Given the lack of a major polling shock, we should expect a continuation of the recent gradual decay or a slight stabilization, worth perhaps -0.1 to -0.3 points.

3. Pre-mortem. Assume your answer turns out badly wrong. Write the most likely reason, then correct for it.
If the forecast is badly wrong, it is likely because the smoothed model "caught up" to a sharper underlying shift in the rolling panel (such as a delayed reaction to a specific controversy not fully captured in the Wikipedia digest) or hit a resistance floor and bounced back towards the low -23s. To correct for this, the standard deviation must generously account for the historical ~0.6 to 0.8 week-to-week volatility. 

4. Calibrate. Your sd should be wide enough that the true value falls inside one sd about two thirds of the time. Check it against how much this series actually moves between releases.
